title: Load Orchestration Run Sequencer & Thermal-aware Batching Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a practical playbook for orchestration of throughput benchmarking runs with two primary goals: 1) maximize inter-run repeatability for long-run throughput baselines, and 2) avoid spurious artifacts caused by hardware thermal cycling and cross-run contention. It complements our existing harness docs by focusing on run sequencing, spacing, and GPU-aware pacing rather than microbench or warmup details alone.

When to use this:
- Multi-run experiments intended to generate release-quality throughput curves (sustained RPS vs latency)
- Capacity planning where runs span hours and need thermal stability guarantees
- Comparing model variants or quantization profiles while avoiding thermal confounds

Assumptions and invariants:
- All experiments use the canonical loadbench client and instrumented server endpoints (tracing + per-token metrics).
- Nodes expose thermal metrics (GPU core temp, power draw) via the monitoring agent. If a node lacks telemetry, flag it on the run and exclude data from final aggregation.
- The environment should be controlled (no infra autoscaling, node eviction, or other external jobs during a benchmark).
- Artifact collection includes raw loadgen logs, node-level telemetry, kernel-level profiler captures for representative windows, and a small sample of raw traces (10-30 requests).

Run-sequencer overview (high level):
1) Preflight: Validate model binary, container image hash, and node allocation. Record image:gitsha and kernel/driver versions.
2) Thermal priming pass: short, conservative load to push GPUs into normal operating range without sustained high-power saturation. This gets thermal state consistent across nodes.
3) Cooldown window: brief steady low-load period to equalize temperatures across nodes (if needed).
4) Main ramps: scheduled single-run or batched-run experiments with explicit inter-run spacing determined by observed thermal drift from priming.
5) Long-run steady windows: for each main run, capture a sustained plateau (recommended 45–90 minutes) depending on target occupancy.
6) Post-run drain and capture: short tail-capture of traces + final telemetry snapshot.

Thermal-aware sequencing heuristics (novelty):
- Prime-to-target ratio: run a 3–5 minute priming pass at 40–60% of target concurrency to bring temp within ~5°C of expected steady state.
- Thermal gap scheduling: if node delta_temp (current minus baseline) > 8°C after a run, automatically insert a cooldown gap scaled with delta (min 2m, max 15m). This avoids chaining heat-accumulation across variant comparisons.
- Run-slicing: for very long experiments (>= 2h), split into contiguous slices (e.g., 30m slices) and verify slice-to-slice repeatability before merging. If slice variance > 6% for p50 throughput, mark run noisy and repeat.

Loadgen configuration templates (examples) – adapt fields to runbench YAML: 

# example-run-template
concurrency: 256
arrival_pattern: paced
sequence_length: random(16,512)
payload_profile: prompt-heavy
batching: auto
kv_cache: enabled
streaming: false
run_duration: 00:45:00
warmup: 00:05:00  # used for per-run micro-warmup inside the harness
metrics_interval: 15s
notes: "thermal-aware orchestration enabled"

Reproducibility checklist (pre-run):
- [ ] Confirm image:gitsha and model hash in run metadata.
- [ ] Tag run with experiment-id and seeded RNG value.
- [ ] Confirm node telemetry agent running and time-synced (ntp/chrony).
- [ ] No other batch jobs on nodes; confirm with `kubectl top` / node audit.
- [ ] Baseline ambient temperature recorded.

Artifact collection (must capture):
- loadbench client logs (stdout/stderr) and per-request logs
- server side p99/p50 latency histograms, token emission times
- node telemetry: GPU temp, power, clock frequencies, CPU temps, fan speeds, node-level thermal events
- kernel-level profiler captures (NVIDIA Nsight/pcap equivalent) for 3 sample windows per run
- run metadata.json (image, model hash, driver versions, seed, config)

Analysis and acceptance criteria:
- Primary metric: sustained tokens/sec (aggregated across nodes) during the middle 50% of run duration. Use trimmed mean to remove transient tails.
- Secondary metrics: median latency of end-to-end response, p95 token emission latency, and error rate.
- Thermal sanity: discard runs where any GPU exceeds a thermal trip threshold (configurable per node/cartridge).
- Repeatability gate: for comparative runs, require <3% relative delta between two independent runs for the same config before accepting a conclusion. Otherwise, label as noisy and re-run.

Observability knobs to capture noise sources:
- Host-level jitter: capture context-switch rate, CPU steal time, and IO wait (iowait).
- Network-induced noise: round-trip latency to model store and to control plane. Tag runs with network spikes >3 sigma.
- Kernel throttles: capture any dynamic clock changes. If a GPU frequency is oscillating during a plateau, annotate and consider run invalid for throughput claims.

Example orchestration flow (command sketch):
1) preflight.sh --exp $ID --image $IMAGE --nodes node-a,node-b,node-c
2) runbench orchestrate --exp $ID --sequence priming,cooldown,main_slice_1,main_slice_2 --thermal-policy auto
3) collect-artifacts --exp $ID --dest s3://bench-artifacts/$ID/
4) analysis/agg.py --input s3://bench-artifacts/$ID/ --out results/$ID-summary.json

Troubleshooting guidance (common failure modes):
- High variance across slices: inspect per-slice telemetry for fan speed or driver reboots. If found, tag nodes and re-run on clean allocation.
- Gradual throughput decay within a run: likely thermal throttling or memory pressure. Compare GPU clocks and power draw across run timeline.
- Spiky latency during plateau: check network and CPU steal; replace load generator if it shows elevated tail latencies.

Practical notes and experiments we've tried (lessons learned):
- Long contiguous runs on identical nodes mask some differences due to accumulated heat; comparing variants immediately back-to-back without cooldown created false positives for faster variants (they were simply measured while hotter).
- Short, repeated slices with enforced cooldown produced more consistent comparisons even if the total wall time was longer.
- In noisy clouds, a small number of quick warmup-only runs on freshly provisioned nodes helps detect early misconfigurations (drivers, MIG partitions) before committing to long runs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact thermal thresholds per GPU family and codify into the orchestration policy (requires small calibration sweep per fleet).
- Explore shadow-run approach: run a low-priority background workload during main run to simulate multi-tenant noise for a subset of experiments.
- Integrate model-level perf counters (attention kernel throughput) into run artifacts for deeper correlation.

Appendix: quick analysis heuristics
- Use the median of the middle 30% of tokens/sec samples as the canonical value for reporting.
- If two runs have median difference in tokens/sec but overlapping bootstrap CI, mark as indistinguishable.
- Produce per-node scatter plots of temp vs tokens/sec and look for slope > 0.5 tokens/sec per degC as a red flag.

If you want, I can convert the heuristics above into a small orchestrator script (run-seq.py) that reads run YAML, queries telemetry, and applies the cooldown rules automatically. For next steps, we should schedule a short calibration sweep on the test fleet (3–4 GPU types) to generate baseline thermal maps and set per-GPU cooldown multipliers.

Notes to reviewers: this is an iterative playbook — feedback on the cooldown scaling law and the slice-size heuristics especially welcome.
